title: RFK Jr tells US families to vaccinate children against measles amid outbreak
excerpt: Health secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMR
content_html:
Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated against measles, as the surge in infections has reached numbers not seen in the past 35 years.

Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning.

His remark came as the incidence of measles crossed a milestone – the US has now officially recorded 2,371 confirmed infections so far this year, surpassing 2025’s total tally of 2,289.

Taken together, the past two years have seen more measles infections in the US than the rest of the 21st century combined. The last time a greater number of measles cases were recorded in a single year was in 1991.

Kennedy’s statement was extracted from him by Dana Bash, CNN’s host, who invited him to use his “bully pulpit” to talk directly to parents as the new school year approached. She urged him to tell families that they should vaccinate for measles “because it is safe and it will help them save their children’s lives”.

The health secretary replied: “Parents should get their children vaccinated for measles. A measles vaccine is effective, it stops measles in about 97% of the cases. People should get vaccinated.”

Later in the interview he added that people should also get the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, the main protection against the disease that has been a particular target of the anti-vaccination movement.

The health secretary’s call for parents to vaccinate their children for measles contrasts starkly with the many years in which Kennedy has been a leading proponent of misinformation questioning the efficacy and safety of vaccinations. Even since he became the country’s top health official, he has depicted a measles vaccination as a personal choice and claimed inaccurately that the power of the inoculation is waning.

The call also comes late in the day, given the rate at which measles is spreading in the US. The 37 new measles outbreaks that have already been recorded this year are putting the US in danger of losing the measles elimination status that it has held since 2000.

Kennedy continues to shrug off criticism that his work as a prominent vaccine skeptic, both before and after he entered the Trump administration, has exacerbated the problem. Asked whether he took any responsibility for the measles surge, he said: “Absolutely not.”

He went on to blame the outbreaks on religious communities who eschew vaccines and on global health conditions.

Any hope that Kennedy’s measles statement might indicate a change of heart were dashed in the rest of the CNN interview in which he turned combative. Batting off questions from Bash, the health secretary responded with personal attacks.

He accused the CNN host of “saying nonsense”, “repeating like a parrot” and “making assertions you can’t support”. In one especially demeaning remark he said Bash had become “flustered”.

“I’m not flustered at all,” she asserted in a calm voice. “I am frustrated because you are the HHS secretary and you are talking about things that lead to vaccine hesitancy in this country.”

In a further comment dripping with condescension, Kennedy told Bash “you probably don’t understand this because you’re not a scientist”.

The journalist riposted: “But you’re not, either.”

The health secretary’s belligerent approach, in which he at times appeared red-faced while frequently poking his finger towards Bash, attracted the attention of commentators. The journalist Aaron Rupar described the performance as “RFK Jr’s epic CNN crashout” and said in a post on X that Kennedy’s “yelling” sounded like “a rabid dog barking”.

Andy Kim, the Democratic US senator from New Jersey, took from Kennedy’s comments that he and Donald Trump had no plans to prepare for a possible next pandemic. “The only thing they have a plan for is trying to distract you from the fact that they’ve taken away healthcare from millions,” Kim said.

Kennedy used the CNN exchange to spread further misinformation about other aspects of public health. He claimed that both respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) that is a major cause of infant mortality and Lyme disease were caused by manipulation of germs in laboratories.

The suggestion has been contradicted by decades of scientific evidence that suggest they both have natural roots. RSV was initially identified in the 1950s, two decades before such experimentation, known as “gain-of-function” research, started.

During the interview, Kennedy repeated unfounded claims that there was a link between Tylenol use during pregnancy and autism, and poured doubt on the efficacy of vaccines to protect children against Covid-19.

Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union later in the show, Ashish Jha, who advised Joe Biden’s White House on its Covid response, said he was heartened to hear Kennedy say that “every kid in America should be getting the MMR vaccine”. But he added that much else of what the health secretary had said “just isn’t true”.

Jha said that the dramatic rise in measles cases on Kennedy’s watch was not coincidental. “The administration has not done enough to promote vaccines. It has not done enough to highlight the harms that come from measles.”

他发表此番言论之际，麻疹发病率已跨过一个里程碑——美国今年迄今已正式记录了 2,371 例确诊感染病例，超过 2025 年的总感染人数 2,289 例。

总的来说，过去两年美国的麻疹感染人数比 21 世纪其他国家的总和还多。 上一次单年麻疹病例数增加是在 1991 年。

美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 主持人达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash) 摘录了肯尼迪的声明，并邀请肯尼迪在新学年临近之际利用他的“讲坛”直接与家长交谈。 她敦促他告诉家人，他们应该接种麻疹疫苗，“因为它是安全的，并且可以帮助他们挽救孩子的生命”。

卫生部长回答说：“父母应该让孩子接种麻疹疫苗。 麻疹疫苗是有效的，它可以阻止大约 97% 的麻疹病例。 人们应该接种疫苗。”

后来在采访中他补充说，人们还应该接种麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹联合疫苗，这是预防这种疾病的主要保护措施，也是反疫苗接种运动的特定目标。

卫生部长呼吁家长为孩子接种麻疹疫苗，这与多年来肯尼迪一直是质疑疫苗有效性和安全性错误信息的主要支持者形成鲜明对比。 即使自从他成为该国最高卫生官员以来，他仍将麻疹疫苗接种描述为个人选择，并错误地声称疫苗接种的效力正在减弱。

考虑到麻疹在美国的传播速度，这一电话也是在当天晚些时候发出的。 今年已记录的 37 起新的麻疹疫情使美国面临失去自 2000 年以来一直保持的麻疹消除地位的危险。

肯尼迪继续不理睬批评，称他在进入特朗普政府之前和之后作为著名的疫苗怀疑论者的工作加剧了问题。 当被问及他是否对麻疹激增负有任何责任时，他说：“绝对不。”

他接着将疫情的爆发归咎于回避疫苗的宗教社区和全球健康状况。

任何希望肯尼迪的麻疹声明可能表明肯尼迪改变主意的希望都在 CNN 采访的其余部分破灭了，在采访中他变得好斗。 这位卫生部长回击了巴什的提问，并进行了人身攻击。

他指责CNN主持人“胡说八道”、“像鹦鹉学舌一样重复”、“做出你无法支持的断言”。 他在一篇特别贬低的言论中表示，巴什已经变得“慌乱”。

“我一点也不慌张，”她用平静的声音断言。 “我很沮丧，因为你是卫生与公众服务部部长，你正在谈论导致这个国家对疫苗犹豫不决的事情。”

肯尼迪在进一步的评论中充满了居高临下的态度，他告诉巴什“你可能不明白这一点，因为你不是科学家”。

记者反驳道：“但你也不是。”

这位卫生部长的好战态度引起了评论人士的注意，他有时会红着脸，并频繁地用手指指着巴什。 记者亚伦·鲁帕尔 (Aaron Rupar) 将这场表演描述为“小罗伯特·肯尼迪 (RFK Jr) 史诗般的 CNN 崩溃”，并在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，肯尼迪的“大喊大叫”听起来就像“一只疯狗在吠叫”。

来自新泽西州的美国民主党参议员安迪·金 (Andy Kim) 从肯尼迪的言论中得知，他和唐纳德·特朗普没有计划为下一次可能的大流行做好准备。 金说：“他们唯一的计划就是试图分散你的注意力，让你忽视他们已经剥夺了数百万人的医疗保健这一事实。”

肯尼迪利用 CNN 的交流进一步传播有关公共卫生其他方面的错误信息。 他声称，导致婴儿死亡的主要原因呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）和莱姆病都是由实验室操纵细菌引起的。

这一说法与数十年的科学证据相矛盾，这些证据表明它们都有天然根源。 RSV 最初是在 20 世纪 50 年代被发现的，比这种被称为“功能获得”研究的实验开始二十年。

在采访中，肯尼迪重复了毫无根据的说法，即怀孕期间使用泰诺与自闭症之间存在联系，并对疫苗保护儿童免受 Covid-19 感染的功效表示怀疑。

为乔·拜登领导的白宫应对新冠疫情提供建议的阿什什·贾在节目稍后接受美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 国情咨文采访时表示，听到肯尼迪说“美国每个孩子都应该接种 MMR 疫苗”，他感到很振奋。 但他补充说，卫生部长所说的其他很多内容“都不是事实”。

贾说，肯尼迪任内麻疹病例急剧增加并非巧合。 “政府在推广疫苗方面做得还不够。 它还没有充分强调麻疹的危害。”
